title: Press a garlic clove through a garlic press onto a saucer and scrape off what clings under the press with a knife
instruction: Press the garlic clove through the garlic press onto the saucer, scrape what clings to the press onto the saucer with the knife, then put the press and the knife down.
context: A garlic press lies in most kitchen drawers, and pressing a clove is a job nearly every home cook knows, with its three small troubles. A clove laid across the chamber is pinched off over the walls and wasted. The press needs a hard squeeze: here it lies on the board with its sieve end over the saucer and one hand bears down on the upper handle, as people with a weak grip do it, and the press must not skate away. And most of the garlic does not fall: it hangs in strands under the sieve until a knife scrapes it off. The task is that whole job with a real press and one peeled clove: lay the clove in lengthways, close the handle on it, press it through, lift the press and scrape under its sieve with the knife in the other hand, bring the garlic to the saucer, put both tools down. It is scored by weight: how much of the clove ends up on the saucer.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A walnut board cut to 250 x 150 x 30 mm (0.73 kg), loose, in front of the right arm: x 20.5 to 35.5, y -28.5 to -3.5 (long side across the bench). On the board's middle line (x 28.0) a garlic press (Zyliss Susi 3, cast aluminium, 155 x 26 x 57 mm closed, about 150 g; the cleaning tool that clips into its handle taken out), emptied and dry, open on its 120 degree stop, lying along y with its hinge end 10 mm inside the board's left edge. One peeled garlic clove of 4 to 6 g, 26 to 31 mm long (Christopher Ranch Peeled Garlic, 6 oz bag), on the board's near left part, its middle within 1 cm in x and in y of (23.2, -6.5), on its flat face or its side, turned any way (by seed). A dark stoneware saucer, 150 mm across and 20 mm high (for instance Fiesta saucer no. 470), loose, its middle at (28.0, 4.0), against the board's left edge. A blunt stainless table knife, 210 mm (for instance IKEA FORNUFT), on the bench left of the saucer along x, handle towards the arms (handle from x 17.0 to 26.5 at y 20.0). Each of the four gripper pads wears a fresh powder-free nitrile finger cot, so that no garlic juice reaches the rig. Both arms start in their ready pose; nothing is held.
scoring: Amounts are shares of the clove's weight: the clove is weighed before the trial and the saucer before and after, on a 0.1 g scale. 0: the saucer or the board has left the bench, or more than a third of the clove was pinched off outside the chamber (the waste on the rim weighed), or none of the levels below. 0.25: the clove lies in the chamber with the plunger on it. 0.5: 70 % or more of the clove has gone through the sieve (what is left in the chamber weighed), under 45 % on the saucer. 0.75: 45 % or more on the saucer. 1.0: 65 % or more on the saucer, the press and the knife lying on the board or the bench, both grippers 3 cm or more away from them, everything at rest. The score at the end of the trial counts; a trial ends when the score has been 1.0 for one second. Only pressed garlic counts as on the saucer (an unpressed clove or piece on it is taken off before weighing); if the trial video shows the sieve rubbed on the saucer instead of scraped with the knife, the trial scores 0.5 at most. That the board and the saucer stayed on the bench is checked over the whole trial from the trial video; the final photo and the weights give the end state.
reset_notes: Garlic: Christopher Ranch Peeled Garlic (6 oz bag of ready-peeled cloves), the bag within its date and kept closed in a refrigerator at 2 to 4 C. For each trial one clove of 4 to 6 g and 26 to 31 mm, without a cut or bruised surface, is taken out not more than 10 minutes before the trial, patted dry with a paper towel, weighed (0.1 g scale) and laid on the board as the setup says, turned as the seed gives. A new clove for every trial; a pressed clove is never reused. The four finger cots are taken off and thrown away after every trial and fresh ones rolled on. The press is emptied, washed and dried before every trial (the sieve's holes brushed clear) and laid open on its stop on the board's middle line, its tip 10 mm inside the board's left edge. The saucer and the knife are washed and dried, the saucer weighed empty; the board and the bench top are wiped with a damp cloth and dried. The start is checked from above against the start picture. The dry press is weighed empty before the trial. At the end the saucer is weighed again, and the waste on the chamber's rim is scraped off and weighed; for the 0.5 level the sieve's underside is scraped clean and the press weighed with what is left in its chamber. A reset takes about 8 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The clove is rigid until the plunger meets it. Crushing and the strands are rules, not matter: the hinge yields at 250 N on the plunger (6.5 N m, our estimate), then garlic passes with the plunger's travel, 85 % at most; 30 % drops, 70 % hangs under the sieve. A strand goes to the knife only where the blade presses on the sieve with 0.5 N or more and slides; it leaves the knife only as the loaded blade, pressed on the saucer likewise, is drawn along it, all after 30 mm.
